title: Edge-Native Multimodal RAG: Hardware-Aware Quantization and Architectural Optimization for Consumer GPUs
abstract: arXiv:2611.14924v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deployment of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for Edge-AI is constrained by memory and bandwidth limitations. A standard 7B parameter model consumes 14 GB Video Random Access Memory (VRAM) in half-precision (FP16), precluding co-location of vector indices and Key-Value (KV) caches. This paper presents an engineering integration and empirical evaluation of a multimodal RAG framework optimized for consumer-grade Turing hardware (e.g., NVIDIA Tesla T4). Our system-level analysis identifies a critical trade-off: while generative pre-trained transformer quantization (GPTQ) offers superior throughput (51.6 tok/s), it exhibits significant context instability at 2048+ tokens on Turing architectures. Conversely, NormalFloat 4-bit (NF4) maintains robust long-context performance with viable latency (81 ms/tok). By coupling NF4 with a decoupled Florence-2 vision integration, we achieve visual reasoning with only 430 MB VRAM overhead. Furthermor

tldr: 该论文针对消费级GPU提出了一种硬件感知量化的边缘原生多模态RAG框架，实证表明NF4量化在Turing架构上比GPTQ具有更稳定的长上下文表现，并通过解耦的Florence-2视觉集成仅以430 MB显存开销实现视觉推理。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a hardware-aware quantization and architectural optimization strategy for edge-native multimodal RAG on consumer GPUs, empirically showing that NF4 quantization offers more stable long-context performance than GPTQ on Turing architectures while enabling visual reasoning with only 430 MB VRAM overhead via decoupled Florence-2 vision integration.
